The '''Continuation War''' was the postwar conflict fought from 3 December 1949 to 6 February 1951 after the formal end of the [[Avant Great War]]. It involved rogue military elements of the defeated [[Vesperan Empire]], loyalist commanders, isolated colonial garrisons, and client-state remnants that refused to accept the United Alignment victory.

== Background ==

The Vesperan Empire collapsed as a central state in 1949, but its military and administrative system did not disappear at once. Some commands surrendered to the [[United Alignment of Nations]], while others attempted to preserve local control, destroy records, evacuate elites, or regroup in former imperial territories.

The result was a scattered but dangerous conflict across several regions, including parts of [[Volgastan Baathist Republic|Volgastan]], [[Empire of Khalindar|Khalindar]], and [[Kingdom of Mariposia|Mariposia]].

== Nature Of The Conflict ==

The Continuation War was not a second world war. It was a series of linked counter-insurgency, siege, occupation, naval interception, and demobilization campaigns. United Alignment forces tried to disarm Vesperan remnants while local independence movements and provisional governments fought to secure postwar authority.

Vesperan loyalists relied on fortified depots, remaining airfields, colonial police networks, naval escape routes, and loyal client units. Their resistance worsened famine, displacement, and reconstruction problems in areas already devastated by the Great War.

== End And Aftermath ==

By 6 February 1951, organized Vesperan resistance had been defeated or absorbed into local postwar conflicts. The end of the Continuation War allowed the victorious powers to move from emergency occupation to legal settlement.

The conflict shaped the weak enforcement style of the postwar order. The victorious powers wanted stability, but they were exhausted by war and reluctant to create a stronger world government. This helped produce the limited Istragarde framework.
